findings.title: Clear loading when the final current-session request is canceled
findings.trigger: A caller starts a loading-enabled request through the exported shared client. The caller aborts it without replacing it. No later response or independent loading reset occurs.
findings.impact: The request sets isLoading=true. The new cancellation return skips loading cleanup. Actual public Service/getService execution rejects ERR_CANCELED on both revisions. Main clears loading and removes PageLoader. Candidate retains loading and PageLoader. Credentials and error state remain unchanged. Ordinary production frequency remains unknown.
findings.fix: Preserve stale-session isolation. Track current-session loading work through cancellation and settlement. Clear loading when no current loading request remains. Keep loading active while a replacement request remains pending. Do not add a bare unconditional loading=false dispatch.
findings.verification: Run canonical DEL14 and DEL19 through real Axios. Assert final cancellation clears loading without credential or error changes. Assert cancellation of request A preserves loading while replacement request B remains pending. Keep stale-session controls passing.
unverified_conditions: Current local admin callers normally replace canceled work. No ordinary final-abort GUI gesture was identified.
Both retained browser result user agents indicate headless Edge. No native lifecycle or deployed-frequency claim follows.

findings.title: Allow a scheduled acquisition when its callback runs slightly late
findings.trigger: A visible current session has access and existing refresh credentials that expire together in sixty seconds. The scheduled acquisition callback runs one millisecond after its intended access-minus-twenty-five-second deadline. No activity or visibility transition intervenes.
findings.impact: The callback sees 24999 milliseconds of access validity and skips acquisition. At the shared expiry, candidate disables Extend and starts Logout. Main acquires replacement refresh and keeps manual recovery available. The same initial credential hashes and claims were recorded on both revisions. Candidate sends two logout requests and clears the session. The state and clock displacement are synthetic; natural occurrence was not observed.
findings.fix: Separate eligibility for a previously scheduled acquisition from late page-return replay. Allow slight callback delay while credentials remain valid. Keep stale-session isolation, pending-request reuse, expiry reconciliation, and late-return cutoff behavior. Do not invent a fixed grace period without policy evidence.
findings.verification: Run canonical DEL20 against both exact revisions with identical initial credential claims. Assert replacement refresh, enabled Extend, no logout requests, and authenticated state. Retain hidden-return, valid-refresh, expired-refresh, and overlapping-request controls.
unverified_conditions: Controlled clocks model lateness. No native timer jitter distribution was measured.
Matching expiry is a synthetic valid frontend state. Independent provider deadlines support compatibility as an inference. No natural occurrence was observed.
The experiment proves recovery availability and forced logout. It does not execute a manual Extend click or a live provider.
